summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5, an updated Sonnet-class model with improved agentic, coding and reasoning performance approaching Opus-class levels, priced at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens.

mechanisms.reason: A customer testimonial states the model achieves the same output quality with fewer steps, implying reduced compute per unit of work, though this is not a lab-stated efficiency technique or industry figure.
mechanisms.quote: Claude Sonnet 5 gets more done with less. Same output quality, fewer steps to get there.

practices.reason: A new released model shows stated evaluation gains in agentic tool use, coding and reasoning over its predecessor, directly changing what teams could deploy in production.
practices.quote: It’s a substantial improvement over its predecessor, Sonnet 4.6, on important aspects of agentic performance like reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work

practices.reason: The document details specific transferable evaluations (BrowseComp, OSWorld-Verified, a Mozilla-collaborated exploit-development test) that an engineering team could adapt to assess their own systems.
practices.quote: Scores measuring models’ success at developing exploits for software vulnerabilities in Firefox 147 (this evaluation was developed in collaboration with Mozilla ; all vulnerabilities have been patched in Firefox 148).

practices.reason: A tokenizer change alters how input maps to token counts, requiring engineering teams to re-check cost and context budgeting when migrating to the new model.
practices.quote: Sonnet 5 is an upgrade to Sonnet 4.6, but it uses an updated tokenizer that changes how the model processes text to improve performance ... roughly 1.0–1.35× depending on the content type.

practices.reason: The evaluation methodology references compaction and programmatic tool calling as techniques for handling very large token budgets, which is directionally relevant to agent orchestration design but not fully specified here.
practices.quote: which used a 10M token budget with compaction and programmatic tool calling

notable_reason: A major Sonnet-family model release narrowing the capability gap to Opus-class models with concrete evaluation data and pricing, relevant to anyone tracking frontier model progress.
